question:
A 15-year-old boy comes to the physician because of severe muscle cramps and pain for 3 months. He first noticed these symptoms while attending tryouts for the high school football team. Since then, he becomes easily fatigued and has severe muscle pain and swelling after 10 minutes of playing. However, after a brief period of rest, the symptoms improve, and he is able to return to the game. Two days ago, he had an episode of reddish-brown urine after playing football. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical and neurological examinations show no abnormalities. Serum creatine kinase concentration is 333 U/L. Urinalysis shows:
Blood 2+
Protein negative
Glucose negative
RBC negative
WBC 1–2/hpf
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?"?

options.ope: CTG repeat in the DMPK gene

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Exercise-induced muscle cramps and pain" -> "Fatigue and muscle pain after physical activity" -> "Reddish-brown urine after exertion" -> "Serum creatine kinase concentration elevated" -> "Urinalysis showing blood 2+" -> "Possible myoglobinuria" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Exercise-induced muscle cramps and pain" -> "Fatigue and muscle pain after physical activity" -> "Reddish-brown urine after exertion" -> "Serum creatine kinase concentration elevated" -> "Urinalysis showing blood 2+" -> "Rhabdomyolysis" -> "Possible myophosphorylase deficiency" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is myophosphorylase deficiency (Glycogen storage disease type V, McArdle disease). The patient's presentation of exercise-induced muscle cramps, fatigue, muscle pain, reddish-brown urine after exertion, elevated serum creatine kinase, and urinalysis showing blood 2+ is highly suggestive of myophosphorylase deficiency, leading to rhabdomyolysis. The evidence path of 'Urinalysis -> Rhabdomyolysis' supports this conclusion.
analysis: The patient's presentation of exercise-induced muscle symptoms, elevated serum creatine kinase, and urinalysis findings of blood 2+ point towards a glycogen storage disease. Among the options provided, myophosphorylase deficiency (Glycogen storage disease type V, McArdle disease) aligns best with the clinical picture, explaining the exercise intolerance, muscle pain, and reddish-brown urine after exertion.
